newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP calls for women-friendly public transport.
newsitem.headline: EP calls for women-friendly public transport.

text.p: Euro-MPs complained on Thursday that European Commission suggestions for improving Europe's public transport systems did not adequately address the specific needs and fears of women.

They agreed with the Commission about the importance of encouraging people to use public transport, so as to reduce the road congestion and environmental damage caused by the ever-increasing use of private cars.
But they said the Commission's Green Paper should have looked beyond the problems of conventional public transport systems, which cater essentially for regular commuters.
The discussion paper -- COM(95)601 -- should have looked more closely at the difficulties facing people, often women, whose travel patterns and needs were more irregular, Euro-MPs said in a report.

"Women's travel patterns and needs are often different from men's, either because of the nature of their work... or their domestic responsibilities...or indeed because of their own security needs given their greater fear of attack while on public transport," the report said.
It said unreliable off-peak services seriously affected women, who made up over 80 percent of part-time workers and often juggled their job with caring for children or elderly relatives.
Euro-MPs were pleased the Green Paper suggested ways of making access to stations and vehicles easier for the disabled and elderly and said women should have more access to such special facilities.

"It is almost always a women one sees struggling down the stairs to a station platform or up the ramp onto a tram, with shopping, baby and a pushchair, while trying to find an extra hand to reach for ticket or change," the report said.
According to the parliament's women's affairs committee, some women have been refused the use of the special disabled access to the new Eurostar train service between Britain and France.
